title: Urgent: resolve RBAC replication suppression and audit telemetry loss during async KMS rewrap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A large enterprise customer on a Private deployment (VPC) reported periodic tenant-level authorization failures and missing audit events during a scheduled KMS envelope rotation. Symptoms: users suddenly lost access to a small subset of routes for 2-10 minutes; control-plane audit logs for corresponding authorization decisions were missing or delayed. The issue correlates with our async KMS rewrap job and an internal RBAC replication path that marks rolebindings as 'stale' until the new key metadata is available.
root_cause_analysis: When envelope rewraps occur, the rewrap job updates key metadata asynchronously. Under sustained message throughput the audit-event publisher encountered transient decrypt failures (old envelope headers) and backpressure in the message queue caused drop-on-overflow behavior for non-idempotent telemetry events. Simultaneously, the RBAC replication worker used a fast-path that temporarily suppressed rolebinding writes while it awaited confirmation of key-version propagation, which led to a window where tenants lacked an authoritative rolebinding in the control-plane cache. The combination produced short-lived access denials and missing audit entries for those requests.
impact_details: Impacted customer: FinanceCorp (Private deployment in us-west-2). Observed: ~7 distinct tenant groups affected, peak duration ~8 minutes, ~1400 failed auth checks, ~460 missing audit events. Support ticket: CUST-8831. Potential wider risk: other private clusters with high-throughput rewrap schedules could see similar windows.
fix_summary: Implement an urgent patch that (1) makes audit-event publishing resilient to decrypt race by making publisher idempotent + retry with exponential backoff and extended TTL on the queue, (2) change RBAC replication worker to hold a light-weight read-locked tombstone instead of suppressing writes until key metadata confirms, ensuring rolebindings remain authoritative during rewrap, (3) add explicit key-version header to outgoing events and bump event envelope to v2 to avoid decrypt ambiguity, (4) increase queue retention/size and switch drop-on-overflow to slow-down backpressure for telemetry events during rollouts.
changes: code: control-plane/rbac/replicator: hold 'in-flight' tombstone and write idempotent rolebinding updates (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4861)
code: telemetry/publisher: add idempotent publish with retry and key-version header (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1298)
infra: increase queue retention to 48h and change behavior to pause producers rather than drop events (k8s helm chart PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-charts/pull/764)
ops: add canary rollout policy: one private cluster -> 5 customers -> global (Console rollout rule: canary-rb-2026-03)
tests: integration: simulate rewrap + high-throughput to validate no auth gaps (CI job: rewrap-rbac-sim)
docs: KB: drafted customer-facing communication and internal runbook (links below)
